items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Cliff Leeman was there for a while... And Eddie Safranski was playing bass... Claude Williamson was the piano player.

ctx.x: Who else was in that band?

Well, let's see. Tiny -- well, Cliff Leeman was there for a while, but then Tiny Kahn took over on the drums, a beautiful man, left us very prematurely. And Eddie Safranski was playing bass, and Carlos Vidal had the bongos and the conga, mostly conga. And Claude Williamson was the piano player. And we had, let's see, Obie Masingill, Dick Kenney -- the other couple of trombone players escape

me. Let's see, there was Lenny something playing the alto saxophone player. Dick Hayfer, tenor. Dave Matthews, tenor. No, Dick Hayfer took Dave Matthews place. Kurt Bloom was playing the other tenor, and Reuben Leon, who's now a union official in L.A. Everybody gets old, don't they? Well, that's about it. The trombones -- I can't remember the other two. Oh, Kenny Matlock was one of them, and -- but it was a real -- but I've got to tell you something about that band. As great as that trumpet section was and as…

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: My association with Charlie Barnet was 1940. The last of '39 and '40 -- and he gave me all the freedom in the world... I wanted Charlie Barnet who just said play

ctx.x: Well, how about your relationship with the bands that you played in? You played in a lot of bands where there weren't any black musicians in them at all.
That's right, but I was also with Charlie Barnet when we had a third of the band was black.
But before you get to the black bands, the ones you played in that were all white, what were your feelings?
